name: Row-aware Hadamard tightening of the full N=1 finite inverse radius

statement.latest: R_j\ge\|J_{0,j*}\|_1,\ H_j\ge\sup_{x\in B}\|D J_{j*}(x)\|_{\infty\to1}\;\Longrightarrow\;\|J_0^{-1}(J(x)-J_0)\|_\infty\le r\sum_j\left(\prod_{k\ne j}R_k\right)H_j;\quad r=\frac{1}{2\sum_j(\prod_{k\ne j}R_k)H_j},\quad 10^{-3878}<r\le10^{-3877}
statement.note_ascii: on the already-certified full N=1 49-dimensional symmetry slice, retain one Jacobian-row and Hessian-row majorant per selected Taylor observation instead of replacing every row by the largest row; the reproduced bound has a 3878-digit denominator versus 7934 digits for the uniform-row proof, a 4056-decimal-order improvement in the power-of-ten radius bracket, while keeping q<=1/2

definitions.J_0: integer-row-scaled selected 49x49 shell-energy Taylor-jet Jacobian at the small-integer N=1 center
definitions.R_j: finite certified l1 majorant for selected Jacobian row j at the center
definitions.H_j: finite certified Jacobian-row variation majorant per unit infinity-radius on the enclosing norm-4 box
definitions.C_j: row-aware cofactor bound product_{k != j} R_k
definitions.r: strictly positive finite state-space radius chosen so the preconditioned Jacobian defect is at most one half

parents.evidence: the 49-dimensional local inverse chart and nonzero integer-scaled determinant are already certified
replaces 49*Jmax^48*Hmax by the row-aware sum of cofactor and Hessian products while preserving q<=1/2; reproduction reports denominator digits 7934 -> 3878
the rigorous radius bracket improves by 4056 decimal orders but remains far below practical measurement scale, so the entrywise-preconditioned frontier remains open

origin.source: github.com/morrocwi/readout-problem-navier-stokes/reproduction/checks/check_volume7_eps18_n1_rowwise_radius.py; reproduction ledger run 2026-09-10 reports inverse-bound digits=3871, radius-denominator digits=3878, q<=1/2 and 4056-order bracket gain

claim_boundary: Finite N=1 tightening only. It improves a rigorous positive-radius lower bound, not the actual conditioning of the inverse. The certified radius remains astronomically small, is not a practical sensor/noise tolerance, does not certify global branch uniqueness, does not extend automatically to arbitrary N, and has no continuum-regularity or Clay implication.
